title: Quadrupolar phase transition in superconducting lanthanum hydride
authors: Abhishek Raghav, Kousuke Nakano, Marco Cherubini, Ryotaro Arita, Michele Casula
abstract: Lanthanum hydride (LaH$_{10}$) has been widely studied for its high superconducting critical temperature of 250 K at about 170 GPa pressure. Although the structural ${R\bar{3}m}$-to-${Fm\bar{3}m}$ transition under pressure connected to the emergence of the superconducting phase in this material is broadly understood, the detailed characterization of its nature and its order parameter are still missing. By applying the cluster multipole moment analysis to the hydrogen sublattice, we reveal that this transition is triggered by a quadrupolar $T_{2g}$ order parameter, and we provide evidence for its weak first-order nature. By performing path integral molecular dynamics coupled to a message-passing atomic cluster expansion (MACE) neural network potential, trained on Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) density functional theory configurations, we show that the collapse of the order parameter at the transition is simultaneously associated with the discontinuous softening of the optical $T_{2g}$ phonons. Their symmetry lets them carry a non-negligible electron-phonon coupling in LaH$_{10}$, while the weak first-order nature of the transition makes them soft. The presence of structural instabilities with low-frequency quadrupolar distortions can be a key ingredient to enhance superconductivity in superhydrides and provides guidance for the discovery of new high-$T_c$ superconductors in hydrogen-rich compounds.
summary: This work investigates the structural transition in superconducting lanthanum hydride ($	ext{LaH}_{10}$) by showing it is governed by a quadrupolar $	ext{T}_{2g}$ order parameter. Using advanced simulations, the authors demonstrate that this transition is weakly first-order and correlates the structural instability with the high critical temperature superconductivity. The findings provide theoretical guidance for designing new high-$T_c$ superconductors.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the nature of the structural phase transition and its connection to high superconductivity in lanthanum hydride ($	ext{LaH}_{10}$).
main_result: The structural transition is driven by a quadrupolar $	ext{T}_{2g}$ order parameter and exhibits a weak first-order character, which is linked to the discontinuous softening of optical phonons.
method: The research employs cluster multipole moment analysis (CMP) and Path Integral Molecular Dynamics ($	ext{PIMD}$) simulations coupled with advanced neural network potentials trained on DFT data.
model_or_system: The system studied is lanthanum hydride ($	ext{LaH}_{10}$), a superhydride known for its high critical temperature ($T_c = 250 	ext{ K}$). The analysis focuses on the structural changes in the hydrogen sublattice under pressure.
key_observables: Quadrupolar order parameter, soft optical phonon frequencies ($	ext{T}_{2g}$ modes), total energy and volume discontinuities across the phase boundary.
important_parameters: High pressures (up to $\sim 170 	ext{ GPa}$) and temperatures; the transition is characterized as weakly first-order.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping structural instabilities via multipole moments and phonon softening, assuming these are key ingredients for high-$T_c$ superconductivity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $	ext{Fm} ar{3}m 	o 	ext{R} ar{3}m$ structural change, showing soft optical phonons that soften, hit a floor, and jump discontinuously with pressure. Other figures map order parameters and phase boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the symmetry breaking using CMP moments to identify the quadrupolar order parameter, corroborates this finding by observing phonon softening/jumps via PIMD simulations, and confirms the weak first-order nature through thermodynamic calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the use of advanced simulation techniques like $	ext{PIMD}$ for anharmonic effects and mapping phase boundaries using order parameters is relevant to understanding quantum many-body dynamics in strongly coupled systems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 Structural transition and phonon softening. a, Fm¯3m and R¯3m structures of LaH10. The top row shows the overall cage structures, and the bottom row depicts the position of H cubes within the La sublattice. The force pattern corresponding to one of the three-fold degenerate soft optical phonons of the Fm¯3m lattice driving this transition is shown in the middle. They exhibit T2g symmetry with characteristic shearing/rotational character. Fm¯3m undergoes a rhombohedral distortion (R¯3m) upon decompression. b, Frequency of the T2g soft optical phonons at Γ, three- fold degenerate, as a function of pressure at various temperatures, computed using displacement- displacement correlator...

Fig. 2 CMP moments averaged over H cubes and over the centroid trajectory. a. Dipolar, b. quadrupolar and c. octupolar moments. Dipolar and octupolar moments are identically zero. Quadrupolar moments, however, are non-zero in the low-symmetry region, and zero in the high- symmetry region. Thus, they serve as a natural order parameter for this phase transition.

Fig. 3 Pressure evolution of the global order parameter across the phase transition. a, Order parameter as a function of pressure at several temperatures. The transition to the high- symmetry phase is defined to occur at the pressure at which the order parameter starts to collapse (dotted line). b, Variance of the order parameter under the same conditions. Fluctuations peak near the transition.

Fig. 4 P −T phase diagram of LaH10. The phase boundary identified using the soft phonon agrees with the one identified using the collapse of the order parameter, showing that the two methods are consistent. Phase transitions as determined in previous reports are also shown for comparison 21,22. Ly et al. 22 identified the low-pressure distortion as R¯3m and placed the transition at ≈96 GPa, which is close to the current work. It should be noted that in both these works, calculations were done over a much coarser P-T grid, making it difficult to determine a precise phase boundary.

Fig. 5 Equation of state across phase transition obtained from PIMD-NPT simulations at 45 K using a 4×4×4 supercell. a, Total energy per LaH10 unit as a function of pressure. Black dashed lines depict the extrapolation of the high-symmetry phase into the low-pressure regime and of the low-symmetry phase into the high-pressure regime. b, Unit-cell volume (relative to the value at 66 GPa) as a function of pressure. Both E(P) and V (P) exhibit two successive slope changes (red dotted line marks the onset), bounding a finite transition region consistent with a weak first-order transition.
